task.description: Review REQ-051's implementation (commit 43ae7ca on branch feature/WF02-REQ051-20260818) against the validated design (lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md). Security review already PASSed (out of scope). Check idiomatic OTP/Elixir usage, purity contract (no Ecto/Repo/Logger/:rand/:crypto), module boundary/scope creep, and decision-record consistency. Also evaluate ELIXIR-DEV's flagged issue: test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs:348 now fails because it asserts the retired REQ-044 stub error for PARALLEL_GATEWAY -- confirm this is a genuinely anticipated, correct consequence of the design (not a real regression) that TEST-DESIGNER should retire/rewrite at Step 3, not something requiring rework here.
acceptance_criteria: New join_counter.ex, and changes to instance_state.ex/transition.ex, follow the module's existing style/idiom conventions (matching req044/req049 precedent).
No scope creep beyond the validated design.
Confirms zero Ecto/Repo/Logger/:rand/:crypto usage anywhere in the diff -- purity contract intact.
Confirms the failing pre-existing test (transition_test.exs:348) is an anticipated, correct consequence of implementing this design, not a real defect.
No contradiction with any docs/migration/decisions/ record.

result.summary: Idiomatic, pure, in-scope implementation matching REQ-044/REQ-049 precedent (plain structs, no Ecto/Ecto.Schema, @spec/@type on every public/private function, per-concept file for JoinCounter, defensive never-raising error paths named per design §7). gateway_role/2's cond-based degree classification is logically equivalent to the design's ordered decision table (verified case-by-case: combined/split/join/pass_through all match). join_outcome/1 is the single shared fire/wait/cancel decision reused by both dispatch_parallel_join/4 and dispatch_cancel_branch/3, exactly as design §4.1 requires (no duplicated three-way branch). VariableMerge.merge/3 is a real call (not a stub/comment), satisfying AC6 at the call-graph level per design §4.3/§6. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, zero warnings. grep for Repo./Logger./DateTime./System.os_time/system_time/HTTPoison/Req./File./:rand./:crypto. across all 4 module files: zero real matches (only hits are the grep command text quoted inside a moduledoc). No Ecto/Repo alias anywhere. No supervision concerns -- this is pure dispatch logic, no process/GenServer/gen_statem involved, so InstanceSupervisor isolation is unaffected (out of this diff's scope). No scope creep: no behaviour/macro/generic plumbing introduced beyond what design doc §1-§11 specifies; REQ-052 is correctly left unaliased/uncalled (design §8's explicit non-dependency, matching REQ-044 SS10/REQ-049 SS6 precedent). No docs/migration/decisions/ contradiction found. Failing test (transition_test.exs:348) verified directly: mix test test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs reproduces exactly one failure, left={:error,{:unknown_node_id,"gw"}}, right={:error,{:gateway_not_yet_implemented,:PARALLEL_GATEWAY,"gw"}}. Traced the cause: the test's fixture is a bare PARALLEL_GATEWAY node with zero edges (out_degree=0, in_degree=0), which gateway_role/2 correctly classifies as :pass_through per design SS3's decision table (out_degree<=1 and in_degree<=1). The :pass_through branch then looks for an outgoing edge to advance along, finds none, and returns the design's own documented defensive path {:error,{:unknown_node_id,node.id}} (transition.ex, dispatch_parallel_gateway/4's :pass_through case; design doc SS3 draws the explicit parallel to :START's SS6.1 defensive nil-edge precedent). This is not a masked regression: REQ-044's PARALLEL_GATEWAY stub is explicitly and intentionally retired by this design (design doc SS7: 'REQ-044's stub is fully replaced'; SS1 module-layout table: 'stub body replaced'). A zero-edge PARALLEL_GATEWAY is no longer an unimplemented-node-type case -- under the new role-based dispatch it is a legitimate (if degenerate) pass-through node, and correctly produces a different, more specific error. The old test encodes REQ-044-era behavior for a node type REQ-051 now fully implements; it is obsolete by design, not broken by a defect. Confirms TEST-DESIGNER should retire or rewrite this specific test case at Step 3 (e.g. split it into a real :pass_through case plus, if REQ-044 coverage of 'not yet implemented' semantics is still wanted for some other node type, retarget it there) -- no ELIXIR-DEV rework required.
